pr_title: Detect CNAME loops in the CNAME cache while trying to resolve
pr_body:
Motivation:

We need to detect CNAME loops during lookup the DnsCnameCache as otherwise we may try to follow cnames forever.

Modifications:

- Correctly detect CNAME loops in the cache
- Add unit test

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/10220
pr_comments: @slandelle I think it should be good enough as `A` would be in the `Set` and so we would break. What I am missing ?
My bad, indeed, I had missed the check on the boolean returned by add.
Then, your call: perfect solution at the cost of extra HashSet allocation vs loop limit without extra allocation?
@slandelle lets keep the set for now...we can add extra options later on. We only need the set if we have more then 2 links in the chain anyway
Can also consider this loop detection algorithm: https://github.com/google/guava/blob/48c7cfd5e38c8492e4356aab5c633254d1ce43be/guava/src/com/google/common/base/Throwables.java#L255

issue_context.title: Netty stops closing sockets and starts burning 100% CPU
issue_context.body:
We develop a pretty high-loaded proxy service based on netty (≈15-20k simultaneous open sockets per process). We encountered a bug when under some rare circumstances netty starts to burn 100% CPU and stops closing sockets, twice during last month and on different hosts.

Stacktrace of the stuck thread
```
"epollEventLoopGroup-7-2" #21 prio=10 os_prio=0 cpu=479213039.41ms elapsed=1475360.37s tid=0x00007f684800f800 nid=0x238 runnable  [0x00007f6835bb1000]
   java.lang.Thread.State: RUNNABLE
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsResolveContext.internalResolve(DnsResolveContext.java:280)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsResolveContext.resolve(DnsResolveContext.java:205)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsNameResolver.doResolveAllUncached0(DnsNameResolver.java:1059)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsNameResolver.doResolveAllUncached(DnsNameResolver.java:1037)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsNameResolver.doResolveUncached(DnsNameResolver.java:941)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsNameResolver.doResolve(DnsNameResolver.java:885)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsNameResolver.doResolve(DnsNameResolver.java:728)
        at io.netty.resolver.SimpleNameResolver.resolve(SimpleNameResolver.java:61)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.InflightNameResolver.resolve(InflightNameResolver.java:100)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.InflightNameResolver.resolve(InflightNameResolver.java:66)
        at io.netty.resolver.dns.InflightNameResolver.resolve(InflightNameResolver.java:51)
        at somepackage.AddressValidationInetSocketAddressResolver.doResolve(AddressValidationInetSocketAddressResolver.java:53)
        at somepackage.AddressValidationInetSocketAddressResolver.doResolve(AddressValidationInetSocketAddressResolver.java:26)
        at io.netty.resolver.AbstractAddressResolver.resolve(AbstractAddressResolver.java:106)
        at io.netty.bootstrap.Bootstrap.doResolveAndConnect0(Bootstrap.java:200)
        at io.netty.bootstrap.Bootstrap.doResolveAndConnect(Bootstrap.java:162)
        at io.netty.bootstrap.Bootstrap.connect(Bootstrap.java:116)
        at somepackage.Http2ProxyHandler.connectAndExec(Http2ProxyHandler.java:233)
```

### Expected behavior
Normally lsof -i -a -n -p gives zero sockets in CLOSE_WAIT state.

### Actual behavior
In our case it shows 20k CLOSE_WAIT sockets (incoming) and the number keeps growing until the open fd limit is reached. It's accompanied by 100% CPU core consumption.

### Netty version
4.1.47.Final
Native netty epoll is used.

### JVM version (e.g. `java -version`)
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 12.0.2+9-Debian-1)

### OS version (e.g. `uname -a`)
Linux hostname 4.9.0-11-amd64 #1 SMP Debian 4.9.189-3+deb9u1 (2019-09-20) x86_64 GNU/Linux
comments: @igor-lukyanov thats interesting... do you have a full thread-dump ? How did you "detect" that the included thread-dump is the one to blame ?

[jstack.txt](https://github.com/netty/netty/files/4539548/jstack.txt)
